title: HC Jeff Hafley - Oct 28 | Press Conference
headline: Kadyn Proctor is in concussion protocol and out of practice; Malik Willis's rushing is being praised as critical, and Jordyn Brooks and Caleb Douglas are getting good reviews.
summary: Hafley opened by saying Kadyn Proctor and an unnamed player called 'Juju' are in concussion protocol after being symptomatic earlier in the week, so they will not practice Wednesday. Everyone else on the 53-man roster is expected to practice, and he clarified that IR players like Trey Moore are not included. He said Jarrett Kingston will work as the third guard and will take reps at guard in practice after Jonah Savaiinaea's injury. On the trade deadline, he declined an either/or answer, saying the team listens on everything but is focused on the current group. He praised the energy coming out of the bye week and stressed starting fast and playing all four quarters. He spoke highly of Jordyn Brooks's physicality, Caleb Douglas's clean play and run-game toughness, and Michael Taaffe's aggressive interception. He credited Malik Willis's running as a critical weapon in the win and said Jacob Rodriguez's four-tackle game reflected limited opportunities rather than poor play. He also reviewed special teams as improved and penalty-free, aside from one hold.

topics.detail: Hafley said the team listens on everything but is sticking with its current roster, declining to give a clear yes or no on veteran additions.
Hafley said special teams improved, with good returns, good field position, and only one penalty (a hold), and he wants to keep developing new players in those units.
He explained that a strong run game creates separation between linebackers and safeties, opening up passing lanes for opponents, so defenders must avoid overaggressive play.
He emphasized that division games matter for a young team, with the focus on development and starting 1-0 in the division.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Oct. 29)
headline: McCarthy praised safety Jaquan Brisker's growing comfort and steady play, and said the injured-reserve players all have a chance to return, ahead of the Week 8 Browns game.
summary: McCarthy said the Steelers value home-field energy at Acrisure Stadium and recognize that winning home games matters, with the Browns coming in as a tough test. On the offense's 27th-ranked red zone production, he pointed to the need to get into scoring position and to convert more trips into touchdowns, and said the week's game plan addresses that. He credited the Browns' habit of winning late in games as a reflection of how the NFL is played today, and said the team has prepared for those moments through training. He praised Jaquan Brisker, saying he is growing more comfortable with his assignments, his play-making ability is real, and the calls reflect that. McCarthy also said the defense's communication is improving every week, starting inside. When asked about the offense's inconsistency across games, he said it is part of the season and that the team is working on it daily, with no specific fix named. He would not name a specific player to expand his role beyond saying the younger player needs to keep practicing hard. On the players placed on injured reserve, he said he believes all of them have a chance to return, and did not suggest any season-ending injuries.

signals.claim: Brisker's role is expanding as he grows more comfortable with the calls and the defense's assignments
signals.note: Coach praised his steadiness, big-play ability, and comfort with the calls, and the reporter noted he played nearly every snap, which supports a stable, high-usage role for IDP and defensive scoring purposes.
signals.quote: you see him more and more comfortable

topics.detail: Asked about the offense ranking 27th in red zone, McCarthy said the team wants to score more touchdowns and that the plan this week addresses it, without naming a specific fix.
McCarthy said winning in the fourth quarter is how the league is played today and that the team has prepared for those moments through training, not a special message.
Asked about the offense being quiet until the fourth quarter in the last Browns game, McCarthy said it is part of the season and that the team has a good plan for this week.
McCarthy said he believes all the players recently placed on injured reserve have a chance to return. He did not name them, so no player-specific timeline was given.
McCarthy stressed the value of the fans and the North Shore environment and said the team wants to win its home games.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald On The Quenton Nelson Trade, Preparing For Week 8
headline: Quenton Nelson is expected to start at left guard and play Monday night, pushing Grey Zabel to right guard and leaving Anthony Bradford displaced; Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr. won't practice Wednesday.
summary: Macdonald said the team is excited to add Quenton Nelson, praised John Schneider's front office for the deal, and called the offensive line's recent game its best of the season. He stressed that the move was not a comment on current players, but acknowledged it affects players who have earned roles. Nelson will play left guard, with Grey Zabel sliding to right guard because of his experience on that side, and Macdonald expects Nelson to play Monday night despite the short transition. Charles Cross is coming along well but won't practice today, and Macdonald said he is not currently headed to injured reserve. Josh Jones will fill in at left tackle as the third tackle. Rashid Shaheed is not expected to practice, and Velus Jones Jr. will also sit out. Drake Thomas will practice, and Macdonald addressed Zach Charbonnet's status only briefly. Macdonald said Bradford has been a starting-level player who will stay ready, though the situation is not easy for him. He also previewed the Chicago Bears, praising their clear identity on offense, defense and special teams, and noted that Montez Sweat's return will help their pass rush.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Jeffery Simmons has been traded, so Keldric Faulk and Oluwafemi Oladejo should see more defensive line snaps; Pollard and Tate sat Thursday and John Franklin-Myers is limited.
summary: Saleh said the injury report was unchanged from Wednesday, with Tony Pollard and Carnell Tate not practicing and John Franklin-Myers limited. He confirmed the Jeffery Simmons trade was real and framed it as a necessary rebuild move after a 1-6 start, saying the team had been losing close games and that other teams had been 'fishing' for players. He said the defensive line will open up opportunities, especially more third-down passing snaps for Keldric Faulk and more time for Oladejo, and that backups deserve a chance. He said Simmons is still battling an injury and he expects him to finish strong, though he declined to detail it. Saleh denied the trade reflected any judgment on Cam Ward, saying it was about building a competitive roster. He also pointed to Cincinnati as the next opponent, and said the team will keep grinding through the week. He expressed confidence in owner Amy Strunk's support and in the organization's direction, and gave a brief scouting note on a newly acquired defensive tackle.

topics.detail: Saleh said the team was shopped to by other teams after a 1-6 start, and that the trade was necessary to add young talent and accelerate the rebuild. He said he was not surprised but that it was the first time it felt real.
Saleh expects defensive coaches to study how opponents slide protection now that Simmons is no longer drawing double teams, and wants backups to take advantage of their opportunities.
Saleh described the newly acquired defensive tackle as a big, athletic player who fits the team's defensive tackle profile, and said the staff is looking forward to seeing him.
